- Firewall and NAT/SNAT expectation for the enclave
- KMS integration notes (we'll use AWS KMS)
- TLS termination model and cert rotation cadence
- Any inbound ports required for metrics/health probes (and the src IP ranges)

I've attached our current network-egress-matrix.xlsx and a high-level Kafka ingress diagram (kafka-ingress-diagram.png) for reference. Sanjay (cc'ed) will be our network lead — he'll handle the configs.

Subject: Re: Tenant Boundary Handoff — Day0 Runbook & Network Evidence

Alex — thanks for the attachments and the clear ask. Attaching our Day0 runbook template (day0-runbook-template.md) to make it easy for you to fill; below is a prioritized checklist so your compliance team can see the minimum acceptance criteria we typically require for Private (VPC/on-prem) activations.

Day0 minimum acceptance (high priority):
1) Egress allowlist: public egress IPs (CIDR) that will be NATing outbound traffic to Redwood endpoints — we prefer stable elastic IPs if available.
2) Inbound health/metrics: allowlist for Redwood agent probes (we require TCP 443 from these ranges - see link) and any SSH bastion IPs if you plan to allow support access.
3) KMS details: key ARN(s), whether cross-account decrypt is allowed, and a contact for key admin.
4) Firewall/NAT: SNAT behavior + sticky NAT expectation (necessary for token pinning). If you have transient SNAT pools, tell us the refresh cadence.
5) TLS/MTLS: confirm if Redwood will terminate TLS at the load balancer or if you require mTLS from client to our runtime; include cert authority details and rotation window.
6) Routing: whether egress uses a proxy (explicit) or direct NAT; if proxy, provide proxy auth model.
7) Evidence: screenshots or syslog snippets showing firewall rule entries + a signed SOC2 or compliance point-of-contact (if available).

Attachments: day0-runbook-template.md (fill and return), plus a short example for how to present IP evidence.

Operational asks / Redwood owners for Day0:
- Ben Carter will run Day0 ops and own the activation playbook.
- Kimberly Park will validate KMS and access controls before cutover.

We'll review the filled runbook and then schedule a 60-minute Day0 dry-run with your network and security teams. If Dec 15 week works, propose Dec 16 or 17, morning PST.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Senior Technical Program Manager — Redwood Inference
Attachments: day0-runbook-template.md
